key_insight: Stoichiometry-preserved ionic clusters, paired with a pretrained MLIP and multi-task fine-tuning, can predict detonation performance of multi-ionic energetic materials before full crystal structures are available.
engineering_relevance: This offers a synthesis-facing screening route for data-scarce energetic materials, helping prioritize promising compositions earlier in the design pipeline.
method: Encode each candidate as a non-periodic stoichiometric ionic-cluster representation.
Fine-tune a pretrained atomistic backbone with an energy-force objective as physical regularization.
Use multi-task fine-tuning to adapt to sparse detonation-velocity labels while retaining transferable structure-chemistry signals.
evidence_signal: The approach was cross-validated on 25 curated perovskite-type energetic materials and achieved 3-point concordance on three newly synthesized ABX4 compounds with a mean absolute error of 92 m·s^-1 without retraining.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on a small, curated dataset, so broader generalization to more diverse chemistries and less structured systems still needs validation.
paper_title: Stoichiometric cluster learning for few-shot property prediction of multi-ionic integrated energetic materials
